title: Stable reduction of curves and stable maps, Part II: moduli of curves and stable compactifications
summary: Partial stable-curve moduli roadmap. The actual polynomial node ring, section ideal and dual have checked coordinate, matrix-presentation and coefficient-universal tensor calculations. Ordinary bidual evaluation now has the explicit inverse F↦F(incl). All eight stages and the reserved key remain partial; arbitrary-module Hom/Ext, relative stable reflexivity, completion and actual family/stack geometry remain required. The polynomial section calculation specifies canonical R-linear tensor–Hom comparisons with every coefficient module, with native scalar actions, signed presentation coordinates, coefficient-module naturality and the ordinary bidual specialization; Ext and completed-local/family conclusions retain distinct inputs. Actual native Hom cochains now specify zero positive cohomology for every coefficient module and correctly signed degree-zero cycles; augmented projective resolutions and the native Ext comparison remain required.
readme: The reader document research/blueprint/readmes/StableReductionPartII.md specifies conventions, source scope, APIs, tests and unresolved supplier boundaries. Stable maps remain in the parent; no stable-map moduli construction is asserted here.

stages.title: The pointed curve moduli problem
stages.description: For every g,n≥0 with 2g−2+n>0 construct the groupoid-valued moduli pseudofunctor of smooth or stable ordered n-pointed genus-g curves over arbitrary schemes, using the parent’s curve-family objects. Establish base-change coherence and effective descent; keep isomorphism groupoids distinct from their sets of isomorphism classes. Construct the universal family with an arbitrary additional section, including sections at a node or coinciding with an existing mark.

stages.title: The unpointed Deligne–Mumford construction
stages.description: For g≥2 construct the tricanonical Hilbert locus with polynomial (6t−1)(g−1), identify its projective-frame torsor and quotient stack, and prove representability, finiteness and unramifiedness of the diagonal. Import the parent’s infinitesimal automorphism vanishing and compute the obstruction space, algebraize versal deformations and obtain independent node-smoothing parameters. Deduce a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension 3g−3 with relative normal-crossings boundary.

stages.title: Universal curves and the full pointed stable range
stages.description: Identify the universal stable curve over the (g,n)-stack with the (g,n+1)-stack by contraction and expansion, including collision and node charts. Prove the inverse comparison and arbitrary-base-change compatibility. Establish the genus-zero base (0,3), the genus-one base (1,1), and the resulting smooth proper Deligne–Mumford theorem of relative dimension 3g−3+n for every stable pair. Compute M₀,₃, M₀,₄ and its compactification and the unstable rational-tail contraction. Separate the explicit polynomial model over every commutative ring: monic normal forms and regularity, matrix exactness, the ordered cokernel maps to J and its actual dual, residue/scalar correction, coefficient flatness and arbitrary coefficient base change. These local calculations do not replace completed-local or global stable-reflexivity/descent inputs. The natural coefficient comparisons are specified as an algebra equivalence for the ring, a canonical tensor-ring action and an R′-linear equivalence for the dual, with identity/composition and actual residue-quotient transport. Coefficient evaluation and the correction K are separately natural; these adapters do not establish completed-local or family descent. The explicit polynomial section ideal is finitely presented over its node ring, without noetherianity. Under flat ambient R→B, identify the actual extended ideal J·B, its B-linear dual and the quotient by multiplication maps canonically. For noetherian R and any ideal I, compare AdicCompletion I D and AdicCompletion I Q with the actual Hom and quotient over AdicCompletion I R. Flatness and faithful reflection are distinct: reflection requires faithful flatness; localization away from the section makes the residue quotient zero. These are specialized uses of pinned finite-presentation Hom and completion algebra. They do not supply Knudsen relative stable reflexivity over S→R, Proposition6’s two-base completion comparison, pointed completed-local normal forms or arbitrary-family/sheaf approximation. The Appendix has now been read; its Bourbaki citation and Proposition7 exercise remain exact open inputs. The coefficient inclusion is identified with the inherited algebra map, evaluation is A-linear, and the actual ideal projection r↦r−ιev(r) supplies the canonical section splitting and flatness retraction. These statements hold over every commutative coefficient ring and do not assert R-linearity. The ordinary polynomial matrix complex and its transpose now have explicit coordinate proofs, and its two cokernel maps to the actual J and Hom_R(J,R) are specified with their negative second generators. Tensoring these complexes and completed-local or family conclusions remain separate. For every coefficient module M, prove the four alternating matrix pairs remain exact after id_M⊗_A−, using the A-flat actual presentation cokernels rather than assuming M flat. Specify the tensorized cokernel equivalences to M⊗_A J and M⊗_A Hom_R(J,R), with representative, inverse and uniqueness formulas. These supply the polynomial universal-acyclicity calculation; actual Hom/Ext, biduality and relative stable-reflexivity/completion interfaces remain separate. For the actual polynomial model, identify the native ordinary R-bidual evaluation with an equivalence whose inverse sends F to F(incl) in the section ideal; use the native dual-of-reflexive instance for its R-linear dual. Keep this algebraic calculation separate from arbitrary coefficient-module Hom exchange, higher Ext and the relative stable-reflexivity/completion descent. Construct the actual canonical R-linear isomorphisms Hom_R(J,R)⊗_A M≃Hom_R(J,R⊗_A M) and J⊗_A M≃Hom_R(Hom_R(J,R),R⊗_A M) for every A-module M. Use the signed presentation coordinate identities C_Jθ_DU(P_D)=−U(p)U(Ψ) and C_Dθ_JU(P_J)=U(p)U(Φ), with universal transpose exactness. Require naturality for every A-linear coefficient map and the M=A native-unit/bidual specialization. Finite-free resolution/Hom cochain and higher Ext interpretation, the relative stable-reflexivity theorem, two-base completion and all completed-local/family comparisons are independent remaining targets. Instantiate native Hom cochain complexes in R-modules with the alternating Ψ/Φ ideal phase and Φ/Ψ dual phase, and identify degree-zero cycles through the actual signed presentations. Distinguish their zero positive native cohomology from the still required augmented finite-free projective-resolution and Ext comparison.

stages.title: Clutching, boundary strata and cotangent lines
stages.description: Lift the parent’s gluing operations to separating and nonseparating morphisms of pointed moduli stacks. Prove they are representable finite and unramified, classify boundary divisors by stable one-edge graphs with their automorphism quotients, and compute the conormal node-smoothing line as the tensor product of the two cotangent lines. Construct marking cotangent lines and their forgetful correction. Do not assert that a whole separating clutching map is a closed immersion, or that normal crossings are globally simple.

stages.title: Coarse moduli, projectivity and full level
stages.description: Construct coarse algebraic spaces separately from the stacks. For g≥2 prove projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse space over Z using pluricanonical direct-image nefness and the ampleness lemma. Obtain a finite surjective normal projective scheme cover. Construct smooth-curve symplectic-similitude level N≥3 over Z[1/N], with a fixed pairing component over Z[1/N,ζ_N]; prove representability, regularity, quasi-projectivity, connectedness and dimension 3g−3, and its smooth projective universal curve. Normalize a chosen projective cover for a stable compactification; never declare naive full level on every nodal curve fine.

stages.title: Hodge determinant and integral Noether comparison
stages.description: Construct the rank-g Hodge bundle and its determinant line on the stable stacks and prove pullback, forgetting and clutching comparisons. For g≥2 construct the integral line isomorphism λ¹²≅⟨ω,ω⟩⊗O(Δ), its base-change compatibility and uniqueness up to the global units ±1 on the universal integral stack. For a generically smooth stable family over an integral noetherian base compute the boundary pullback at a trait as the sum of node thicknesses. An equality in rational Chow groups does not substitute for this integral Picard-group identity.

stages.title: Stable compactifications and Torelli
stages.description: For an integral quasi-projective S over Z or a field with a stable genus-g family (g≥2), produce a dominant finite cover S′→S and a projective integral compactification carrying a stable extension, by retaining the base in a graph closure. Construct the smooth full-level Torelli map and its Cartesian universal-Jacobian comparison, finite fibres with the ±level ambiguity and the genus-two exception. Construct the compactified Torelli map to the minimal Siegel compactification and its Hodge pullback. For maximal variation deduce nefness and bigness of the pulled-back Hodge line, using generic finiteness rather than a globally finite smooth Torelli morphism.

stages.title: Level Picard parameters and consumer interfaces
stages.description: For a fixed genus g≥2, level N≥3 invertible and degree d∈Z define the level-Picard parameter functor and compare it with relative Picᵈ of the universal smooth curve. Keep the fppf-sheafified Picard functor distinct from globally existing line bundles; identify triples only over algebraically closed fields or under the explicit Brauer-obstruction vanishing condition. Export the moduli and family interfaces to the six key-definition consumers, without rebuilding their Hurwitz stacks, mapping-class groups or tautological Chow rings.
